stem: How is population density calculated?

options.rationale: This is not a density measure.

explanation: Density = population ÷ area (people per km²).

stem: Which world region is **sparsely** populated?

options.rationale: This is one of the most densely populated areas.

explanation: Deserts are sparsely populated because of lack of water.

stem: Why is the Nile valley in Egypt densely populated even though it lies in a desert?

options.rationale: Correct: water and soil support farming and settlement.

options.content: It is covered by tropical rainforest

explanation: Rivers in deserts attract dense settlement.

stem: Which area of Zimbabwe is **sparsely** populated?

options.rationale: This is the most densely populated urban area.
This has reliable rain, fertile soils and many towns.
Correct: hot, dry, with poor soils and a history of tsetse fly.

explanation: Low rainfall, heat and disease kept the Zambezi valley sparsely settled.

stem: Which is a **human** factor that leads to dense population?
explanation: Human factors include jobs, transport, services and government policy.

stem: On a dot map, what does a large blank area show?

options.content: An area with no data available
options.rationale: Dot maps show blank areas where few people live.
Cities appear as clusters of dots.
Correct: no dots means very few people.

explanation: Dots represent people; their absence means sparse population.

stem: A choropleth map shows one district in Zimbabwe's dry Lowveld with a high population density. What is the most likely explanation?

options.rationale: The Lowveld has low, unreliable rainfall.
National parks have very few residents.
Correct: irrigation and agro-industry support dense settlement.

explanation: Irrigated estates such as those around Chiredzi and Triangle create local concentrations.
hints: What could support many people in a dry area?

stem: A district has a density of 40 people per km². Why might this figure be misleading?

options.content: Density is always measured in people per hectare
It is the same as the birth rate
options.rationale: Density and birth rate are unrelated measures.

options.content: Most people may live in one town, leaving the rest empty
options.rationale: Correct: density is an average that hides variation.

explanation: An average density can hide clusters and empty areas.

stem: Why do many communal areas of Zimbabwe have high rural population densities, even on poor soils?

options.content: They have the country's richest soils and highest rainfall
options.rationale: Many communal areas have poor soils and low rainfall.

options.content: Colonial land policy confined many farmers to limited land
They contain the country's largest factories

explanation: Historical land allocation, not only physical factors, shapes density.

stem: Population density is usually measured in people per square kilometre.
explanation: True: people per km².

stem: The Congo rainforest is densely populated because it has high rainfall.
explanation: False. Dense forest, leached soils and disease make it sparsely populated.

stem: Match each area with the main reason for its population density.

right.content: Fertile volcanic soils and reliable rain: dense

explanation: Physical factors explain many dense and sparse areas.

stem: Complete the sentence.

payload.template: A map that shades areas according to their average density is a {{blank:a}} map. A map in which each symbol stands for a set number of people is a {{blank:b}} map.

explanation: Choropleth maps shade areas; dot maps use dots for people.

stem: A fictional district has 54,000 people on 1,350 km². Calculate its population density.
explanation: 54,000 ÷ 1,350 = 40 people per km².

stem: A fictional ward has an area of 2,400 km² and a population density of 35 people per km². Calculate its population.
Zimbabwe had about 15.2 million people (2022 census) and has an area of about 390,000 km². Estimate its population density to the nearest whole number.
Explain why the highveld of Zimbabwe is more densely populated than the Zambezi valley.

points.description: Highveld has more reliable rainfall; the Zambezi valley is hot and dry.
Highveld has more fertile soils for farming.
Highveld has cities, industry, mines and jobs / good roads and railways.
Zambezi valley has had tsetse fly and malaria / poor access / national parks and safari areas.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The highveld has reliable rainfall, a moderate climate and fertile soils, and it contains Harare and other towns with jobs, served by roads and railways. The Zambezi valley is hot and dry with poor soils, and tsetse fly and malaria discouraged settlement; much of it is protected wildlife land.

explanation: Contrast physical and human factors in both areas.

stem: Describe the distribution of population in Africa.

points.description: Dense in the Nile valley and delta.
Dense along the West African coast (e.g. southern Nigeria) and in the Great Lakes region (Rwanda, Burundi, Uganda).
Dense in the Ethiopian highlands / South African highveld and coasts.
Sparse in the Sahara, Kalahari and Namib deserts and the Congo rainforest.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Africa's population is concentrated in the Nile valley, along the West African coast especially in Nigeria, around the Great Lakes, in the Ethiopian highlands and in parts of South Africa. The Sahara, Kalahari and Namib deserts and the Congo rainforest are sparsely populated.

explanation: Name places for both dense and sparse areas.
hints: Name dense and sparse regions of Africa.

stem: "Physical factors are more important than human factors in explaining population density in Zimbabwe." Discuss this statement.

points.description: Physical: rainfall and natural regions (highveld dense; Zambezi valley and Lowveld sparse).
Physical: soils, relief, water and disease (tsetse fly, malaria).
Human: towns and jobs (Harare, Bulawayo); mining towns along the Great Dyke.
Human: irrigation schemes (Lowveld sugar estates) overcome physical limits.
Human/historical: colonial land policy produced dense communal areas; national parks keep areas empty.
Supported judgement (e.g. physical factors set the broad pattern but human factors explain many exceptions).

levels.descriptor: Developed, accurate explanation of several relevant points, supported by a located example or the resource, with a clear judgement or conclusion where the question asks for one.
Some explanation of relevant points, partly developed; an example or resource evidence is used in general terms; any judgement is simple or one-sided.
Simple statements or a list of points with little explanation; no example or only a name.

answerSpec.modelAnswer: Physical factors explain the broad pattern: the wetter highveld and Eastern Highlands with fertile soils are densely settled, while the hot, dry Zambezi valley and Lowveld, once affected by tsetse fly, are sparse. However, human factors are very important. Harare, Bulawayo and the mining towns of the Great Dyke have dense populations because of jobs. Irrigation has created dense settlement around the Lowveld sugar estates despite low rainfall. Colonial land policy crowded many farmers into communal areas, some on poor soils, while national parks such as Hwange keep large areas nearly empty. Physical factors set the general pattern, but human factors explain the highest densities and many exceptions, so the statement is only partly true.

explanation: Balance both groups of factors and judge.
hints: Compare physical factors with human factors.

points.description: C has irrigation, so crops do not depend on rain.
The sugar estate needs many workers for growing, cutting and milling.

parts.stem: How many people live in square X?

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the population density of square X.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Give **two** limitations of dot maps for showing population.

points.description: Dots may be placed inaccurately within an area / clusters merge and are hard to count.
Choosing the dot value is difficult: too large hides small settlements, too small crowds the map.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: In crowded areas the dots merge so they are hard to count, and a single dot value cannot show both small villages and large towns well.

parts.explanation: Dot maps are good for pattern, weaker for exact values.

explanation: This item practises using a dot map.
